items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: Sinatra and Ella and, you know, my father

ctx.x: Yeah. Well as you’re saying that I’m thinking about my mom. My mother, who you knew, she knew every song, I think every standard song ever written. She knew them all. She could sing the lyrics. She was not a musician, and she wasn’t a singer, but she would buy these books of lyrics, the hit parade books, I’m talking about from the 1940’s on. And she would look at the lyrics and every song that would come on the radio, anything that would play, bang, she would start singing. Sometimes it would be “mom,” you ©…

know, “please.” Yeah. So a lot of that was growing up and hearing that music. Another advantage if you’re going to play standards, and the kids today don’t necessarily get that in their homes, you know, in the background, you have to seek it out. We didn’t have to seek out that music, it was the music of our lives. That was what we heard. Sinatra and Ella and, you know, my father, another non-musician but he loved Count Basie’s band and all the great big bands and all that. So that’s kind of what we heard.
Were they happy that you became a professional musician?
